title: Event Schema Registry & Contract Testing Platform with Python, Kafka, Apache Avro & FastAPI
problem: Microservice topologies publishing and consuming high-velocity streaming events over Apache Kafka experience catastrophic silent pipeline failures, downstream consumer crashes, and data lake corruption when producer services deploy schema modifications without coordinating changes. Lack of centralized schema governance results in breaking field deletions, incompatible data type mutations, and untraceable payload drift across polyglot service teams. This project builds a production-grade centralized schema registry and event contract testing platform in Python. The system registers and versions Apache Avro schemas, enforces strict compatibility validation rules (BACKWARD, FORWARD, FULL, NONE), assigns global monotonically increasing schema IDs, persists schema definitions in PostgreSQL, provides a high-throughput REST API in FastAPI, and supplies serializer/deserializer interceptors for Kafka producers and consumers.

use_cases.title: Financial Transaction Payment Event Governance
use_cases.first_sentence: Core banking microservices streaming debit card authorization events must ensure downstream fraud detection engines never receive malformed payloads.
use_cases.second_sentence: The schema registry intercepts outgoing payment messages, validating Avro schemas against registered contract versions before publishing to production Kafka topics.

use_cases.title: Continuous Delivery Pipeline Contract Compatibility Gate
use_cases.first_sentence: Platform CI/CD pipelines need automated contract verification to block deployments of producer microservices that introduce breaking schema modifications.
use_cases.second_sentence: The registry CLI runs pre-deployment compatibility checks against existing consumer versions, failing CI jobs with detailed diffs when non-backward-compatible changes are detected.

use_cases.title: Enterprise Data Lake Analytics Ingestion Parity
use_cases.first_sentence: Data engineering teams consuming Kafka topics into analytical warehouses require consistent schema history to maintain partition evolution without table re-writes.
use_cases.second_sentence: The registry assigns unique 4-byte schema IDs embedded in message wire framing, allowing warehouse loaders to parse diverse event versions deterministically.

hard_parts: Implementing comprehensive Apache Avro schema compatibility validation algorithms (BACKWARD, FORWARD, FULL, and transitive variants) according to the Avro specification
Designing confluent-wire-format binary serializers and deserializers that encode a magic byte and 4-byte global schema ID prefix with sub-millisecond serialization overhead
Managing concurrent schema registration race conditions in PostgreSQL to guarantee unique version numbers and avoid duplicate schema fingerprint allocations
Building an automated contract testing suite in Python that simulates evolving producer/consumer deployments across 10 distinct schema lifecycle iterations
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase cleanly separating Avro compatibility algorithms, REST API routers, PostgreSQL storage repositories, and Kafka serializer interceptors
High-throughput benchmark report proving sub-10ms schema validation and registration latency under 500 concurrent registration requests per second

Anti-fake verification script attempting to register an incompatible breaking schema (removing a required field without default value) under BACKWARD mode and asserting HTTP 409 Conflict with detailed field diff

architecture.data_flow: A producer prepares to emit a Kafka event; the serializer checks its local schema cache; if missing, it calls FastAPI `POST /subjects/{subject}/versions` with the Avro schema; the registry queries PostgreSQL for the latest version; the compatibility engine validates that the candidate complies with the subject's mode (e.g. BACKWARD); if valid, it assigns a global schema ID (or returns the existing ID) and persists to PostgreSQL; the producer encodes the magic byte and 4-byte schema ID followed by the Avro binary payload and sends to Kafka; consumer interceptors read the 4-byte ID from the header, fetch the schema from the registry, and deserialize the payload safely.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Transactional unique constraints on (subject, version) and schema fingerprint hashes in PostgreSQL preventing duplicate registrations.
